units: categorical (relative lizard density per plot; GLM with treatment and day, Tukey post hoc)

source.title: Supplementation of Male Pheromone on Rock Substrates Attracts Female Rock Lizards to the Territories of Males: A Field Experiment

method: field experiment: paired plots, rocks painted with ergosterol in dichloromethane versus dichloromethane alone, repeated censuses
conditions: Wild, unmarked lizards at Alto del Telégrafo, Guadarrama Mountains, central Spain (about 1,900 m), May to June 2009. Twelve areas of 15 x 6 m each held two 2 x 2 m plots; one plot per area was randomly assigned to ergosterol (25 g/L in dichloromethane, painted on rocks with brushes) and the other to the dichloromethane control (n = 12 pairs). Seven censuses per day, one every 30 min; treatment applied on four days (27 May, 2 and 3 June, 11 June) plus an initial day. Females were more abundant in treated plots on the third and fourth day (P = 0.007 and P = 0.017) and the treatment x day interaction was significant (F4,44 = 2.83, P = 0.037); 46 females were seen near males in treated plots against 10 in control plots (binomial P < 0.0001). Nulls: the experimental manipulation did not affect male density (P = 0.10) or subadult density (P = 0.54). Counts are relative densities, not individuals; the authors state the method only provided estimations of relative densities. Ergosterol is a measured dose on the rock, not an airborne concentration.
quote: In the field, we added ergosterol to rocks inside the territories of male lizards, and found that this manipulation resulted in increased relative densities of females in these territories.

source.title: Lamp-Lit Bridges as Dual Light-Traps for the Night-Swarming Mayfly, Ephoron virgo: Interaction of Polarized and Unpolarized Light Pollution

method: field experiment: LED torch beamed at the compensatory-flight swarm with a horizontally polarizing filter versus a depolarised filter, alternating, mayflies counted from photographs
conditions: Wild swarms over the Danube at Tahitótfalu, Hungary, 23, 24, 27 and 28 August 2013 (about 99% females in carcass samples). One high-intensity LED torch (UltraFire C8 Cree XM-L T6) on a tripod on the river bank 110 m from the bridge, aimed upstream at the swarm; the polarized filter (white tracing paper plus linear polarizer) and a filter with the order reversed, giving practically unpolarized light described as of the same intensity, were alternated, each in four 100-second runs per night; 10 photographs per session, about 1,500 photographs analysed with custom software, roughly 150,000 mayflies counted (software versus visual counts differed by under 5%). The two lights were not on at the same time and no radiometric value for the intensity match is given in the Methods text read. Mann-Whitney U per night, polarized versus unpolarized: 23 August N = 11582, U = 181, Z = 10.302, p < 0.00001; 24 August N = 22786, U = 674.5, Z = 11.388, p < 0.00001; 27 August N = 5425, U = 303.5, Z = 8.945, p < 0.00001; 28 August N = 93935, U = 8682, Z = 10.465, p < 0.00001. The Figure 4 caption dates the data to 2012 while the Methods give 2013. The same paper's observations of attraction to unpolarized bridge lamps are a separate result.
quote: Depending on the swarming day, the horizontally polarized light attracted on average 5–10 times more mayflies than the unpolarized light.

source.authors: Dacyn Holinda, Joanna M. Burgar, A. Cole Burton
source.title: Effects of scent lure on camera trap detections vary across mammalian predator and prey species

method: field experiment: paired lured and unlured camera-trap stations, detection counts modelled with zero-inflated negative binomial GLMMs
conditions: Free-ranging mammals in Alberta, Canada, February to August in 2015 and 2016. 844 camera stations (404 lured, 440 unlured) at 247 sites, four Reconyx PC900 cameras per site about 600 m apart at the corners of a square, two lured with O'Gorman's Long Distance Call (a skunk and musk blend) in a PVC tube staked 5 m in front of the camera and two without; 120-day survey periods; mammals were detected at 800 of 844 stations, with 7110 detections at lured and 7530 at unlured stations. Zero-inflated negative binomial mixed models with site as random effect; the authors assumed any lure effect lasted the full 120 days and removed zero-inflation from the wolf model. Per-species lured and unlured counts are not reported in the text read. Lure is a commercial product, not a defined compound. Same paper: predators as a group, large and small carnivores and fisher were detected more at lured stations; prey, small mammals and ungulates were not. Fisher: beta = 2.23 +/- 0.36 SE, z = 6.18, p < 0.001.
quote: Scent lure significantly increased detections of predators as a group, including large and small carnivore sub-groups and fisher specifically, but not of gray wolf.

value: wolf urine did not significantly affect red deer behaviour in either the wolf-absent or the wolf-present area

source.authors: Hermine Annette Lisa van Ginkel, Christian Smit, Dries Pieter Jan Kuijper
source.title: Behavioral response of naïve and non-naïve deer to wolf urine

method: field experiment: camera traps at dispensers of wolf urine, water and all-purpose soap, Kruskal-Wallis tests
conditions: Free-ranging red deer, spring 2016, two case studies: Veluwezoom National Park, Netherlands (wolf-absent; 25 locations, 75 plots, 507 trapping days, 69 red deer visits) and Bialowieza Forest, Poland (wolf-present; 20 locations, 60 plots, 415 trapping days, 115 visits). Three treatments per location (wolf urine, water as no-scent control, lemon-scented all-purpose soap as unfamiliar-scent control), plots at least 50 m apart, treatment order randomised within location, one camera per dispenser for seven days; only individuals present more than 4 s were scored. Wolf urine was commercial, from captive animals. Roe and fallow deer were excluded for too few visits. Contrary result: in Poland foraging time was lower on soap plots (H = 7.088, P = 0.029), with a non-significant trend to higher vigilance (P = 0.088); soap had no effect in the Netherlands. Vigilance on control plots was 20% in both areas. Urine dose and release rate not stated in the abstract.
quote: Placing wolf urine did not significantly affect deer behavior in either the wolf-absent or the wolf-present area.
